## Summary

On 2026-09-02 the rebar Gerrit host filled its root volume and took Gerrit offline for about five hours. Recovery enlarged the root volume, but that was only an unwedge; the class was unbounded root-disk consumers plus alarms that could go healthy when the host stopped publishing.

## RCA

Two defects combined:

1. Root-volume consumers had no hard ceilings. Docker/BuildKit, journald, /var/tmp, writable container layers, and review-gate scratch could all consume root without a bounded per-generator cap. One-off pruning or a larger root disk only bought time.
2. Host-published disk alarms treated missing data as non-breaching, so when the host died and stopped publishing, the alarm could reset to OK instead of paging on loss of signal.

Subsequent measurements showed the original failure was not a single static directory: root usage had sawtooth build/deploy bursts, a rising trough during some merge bursts, Docker cache and unaccounted data, /var/tmp residue, and review-gate scratch originally on root. Later live fixes moved scratch to its own volume and installed per-generator caps/alarms.

## Resolution

The incident response and follow-up landed the missing-data alarm fix and the bounded disk-ceiling architecture from epic 6202:

- root/data disk alarms no longer treat missing metrics as healthy;
- review-gate scratch is on a dedicated EBS volume with its own alarm;
- Docker/BuildKit has configured GC/retention and per-generator alarms;
- journald has a storage cap and cap-health alarm;
- /var/tmp cleanup/usage is bounded and alarmed;
- writable container layers/exited-container debris are bounded and alarmed;
- the host-wedged/SSM-ConnectionLost recovery path is documented as an unwedge only.

Live close evidence at 2026-09-08T17:14Z: root 16G/60G (27%); /var/gerrit 13G/50G (25%); /var/lib/rebar/gate-scratch mounted on its own 50G volume at 20G/50G (39%); Build Cache 2.113GB below its 5GiB cap; journald 1.8G; /var/tmp rebar residue empty. Disk-related CloudWatch alarms were OK: root/data/gate-scratch disk, Docker storage/BuildKit/unaccounted/du, journal cap/usage, var-tmp cleanup/usage, and container reaper/stats/writable usage.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] AC1 [non-codebase]: rebar-root-disk-pressure and rebar-gerrit-data-disk-high no longer treat missing data as healthy; missing publisher data pages instead of clearing to OK.
- [x] AC2 [non-codebase]: the disk alarm re-enters alarm when the publisher dies, instead of self-clearing to OK and staying there.
- [x] AC3: the top consumers of the root working set were identified with measured byte totals where available.
- [x] AC4: root usage has bounded ceilings, not merely faster reclaim: the per-generator cap/alarm architecture above is landed and live, and current host measurements prove usage is below those ceilings.
- [x] AC5: the /var/gerrit remediation was completed or explicitly carried by the bounded-ceiling work, so the data volume is not left with the same unbounded shape.
- [x] AC6 [non-codebase]: the wedged-host/SSM-ConnectionLost runbook path records snapshot -> modify-volume -> reboot -> cloud-init growpart as an unwedge requiring follow-up reclaim.

## Close class

env_integration: the bug was a production infrastructure/operations failure, fixed by deployed host configuration, runbooks, alarms, and landed infra support.
## Verification

Checked live on 2026-09-08 with `df -h / /var/gerrit /var/lib/rebar/gate-scratch`, `docker system df`, `journalctl --disk-usage`, `/var/tmp` residue listing, and `aws cloudwatch describe-alarms` for disk/Docker/journal/tmp/container alarms. Plan and completion gates are run before close.
